title: Clarinetists: Piku, McCurdy, Boccage, and Freddie Keppard
summary: Foster compares clarinetists Piku, Charlie McCurdy, George and Charles Boccage and Lorenzo Tio, and says he played occasionally with Freddie Keppard.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Were you with Silstan when Clem Rabin played with him? Yeah. Did Clem sound very much like Piku or?
I said Piku played all together, a different style from them all together.
Well, was Ramon a popular clarinetist in town at that time? Well, Piku was the most popular time. Yeah. Cool. I just wondered because he's out in San Francisco, we're going to have him in the court.
Who were some of the other better clarinetists? You mentioned Charlie McCurdy. How did he play?
He was a number one. He was a number one musician. A number one musician. What I mean by A number one, no sooner they put a piece up in front of him, he don't have to rehearse it.
I know Bunk said he was very good, one of the best. Yeah. George Boccage, did you ever know him or play with him? Yeah.

Yeah. He was a great clarinet player too. Him and Lorenzo Teo on the same style. Played when they got ready. I don't say that they couldn't play. When they played like nothing, well, they just wasn't feeling good. But when they got ready to play, nobody couldn't touch them, black or white.
Boccage was in the Onward band, wasn't he?

Charles Boccage, yeah. You see those fellas like that, those fellas in Manu Peris's time, like I was telling you, like Manu Peris's time and Peter Boccage, Manu Mineta, those fellas are all about the same age. All about the same. Freddie Keppert and them, all those.
I was going to ask you, did you ever play with Freddie Keppert?
Yeah, I played with him, but not a regular man.
He went away from here from pretty young parents. Yeah. Yeah.
